meta.title: Discontinue a product and create its replacement

messages.label: 400 if empty name or price <= 0
messages.note: Caller-supplied values only — no stored data read here.

messages.label: null → 404, or already-discontinued → 400
messages.note: Unknown id or an already-discontinued product short-circuits here, before any write.

messages.label: SaveChangesAsync — both rows in one transaction
messages.note: product.Discontinue() and new Product(replacementName, replacementPrice) both commit in this one call.

cards.title: Why this route is hand-written
items: Discontinuing also creates a named replacement Product — two aggregates in one transaction, which no [CrudAction] can express
The generated Discontinue route is excluded by name (Exclude("Discontinue")) and replaced by this one

cards.title: Already-discontinued is a handler-level failure
items: A second call against the same id returns 400 from the handler ("already discontinued"), not a validator precondition

A generated [CrudAction] route could have expressed this refusal too — as a FluentValidation validator against its generated request, the same way CreateProductRequestValidator and DeleteProductRequestValidator work. It stays hand-written because of the two-aggregate transaction, not because of this rule.

cards.title: What this cannot show
items: A replacement name that collides with an existing product's unique index is not caught by the validator — it reaches SaveChangesAsync and surfaces as an unhandled 500, confirmed live
EfAutoSavePostInterceptor commits once after the handler returns, so a failed insert rolls back the Discontinue() call too — the original product is unchanged on that 500
